findings.summary: Halyard achieves lower test MAE than Tidewell on all five datasets in the suite, with differences ranging from 0.013 to 0.017.
findings.scope: Five multivariate forecasting datasets (Kelso-Grid, Marrick-Traffic, Doveton-Weather, Ashby-Retail, Pell-Solar), horizon 96, test MAE on z-normalized series, mean over 3 seeds.
findings.caveats: No statistical tests were reported, so the consistency of the advantage across datasets is descriptive only; significance is not established.

findings.summary: Halyard also outperforms the seasonal-naive reference on all five datasets, with larger margins than against Tidewell.
findings.scope: Same five datasets, horizon 96, test MAE on z-normalized series, mean over 3 seeds.
findings.caveats: No statistical tests reported; margins are descriptive.

findings.summary: The evidence supports that Halyard outperforms Tidewell across the evaluated benchmark suite, but the claim is limited to these five datasets and this specific setting (horizon 96, z-normalized MAE, 3-seed mean).
findings.scope: The full five-dataset suite under the stated experimental setup.
findings.caveats: No statistical significance tests were provided; generalizability beyond these datasets and settings is not established.

sentences.text: Across the five multivariate forecasting datasets in the suite, Halyard achieved lower test MAE than Tidewell on every dataset, with margins ranging from 0.013 (Kelso-Grid) to 0.017 (Pell-Solar).
Halyard also outperformed the seasonal-naive reference on all five datasets, with larger margins (0.068–0.111) than against Tidewell.

These results support that Halyard outperforms Tidewell across the evaluated suite, but the claim is limited to these five datasets under the specific setting of horizon 96, z-normalized test MAE, and a 3-seed mean, and no statistical significance tests were reported.
